'''Paul Andrew Zeitz''' (born July 5, 1958) is a professor of mathematics at the [[University of San Francisco]] who works primarily in math enrichment.

== Early life and education ==
In 1974, Paul Zeitz won the [[USAMO|USA Mathematical Olympiad]] (USAMO) and was a member of the first American team to participate in the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]] (IMO). The following year he graduated from [[Stuyvesant High School]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.usfca.edu/usfnews/02/03.05.02/fp5.html |title=Professor Teaches Passion for Math |website=usfca.edu |date=2002-03-05 |accessdate=2007-10-31 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20051117033202/http://www.usfca.edu/usfnews/02/03.05.02/fp5.html |archivedate=November 17, 2005 |df=mdy-all }}</ref>

In 1981, he graduated from [[Harvard University]] with a Bachelor of Arts in history.<ref name="Harvard Magazine Proof">{{cite news |last1=Baron |first1=Violet |title=math-kids-facilitator |url=https://www.harvardmagazine.com/2016/08/math-kids-facilitator |access-date=31 July 2025 |work=Harvard Magazine |issue=September–October 2016}}</ref> After graduating he taught high school math for six years in San Francisco and Colorado Springs. He then went to [[UC Berkeley]] and obtained a PhD in mathematics in 1992.<ref name="AIM">{{cite web |title=The Teacher's Circle, August 14–18, 2006 |url=https://www.aimath.org/~circle/theteacherscircle.org/circle/Paul_Zeitz.pdf |website=American Institute of Mathematics |access-date=31 July 2025}}</ref>

== Career ==
After graduating from UC Berkeley, Zeitz became a professor at the [[University of San Francisco]].<ref name="AIM" />

In 2015, Zeitz co-founded [[Proof School]], which is a private school for middle and high school grade levels that is focused on math. Proof School teaches mathematics from the perspective that it is a "joyous art form."<ref name="Harvard Magazine Proof" /><ref>{{cite web |last1=Mandal |first1=Sayantika |title='Joyous Artform' |url=https://www.usfca.edu/news/joyous-artform |website=University of San Francisco College of Arts and Sciences |access-date=31 July 2025}}</ref> Zeitz also co-founded the Bay Area Mathematical Olympiad in 1999 and the San Francisco [[Math circle|Math Circle]] in 2005.<ref name="AIM" /><ref>{{cite web |title=Our Mountain Math Guides |url=https://www.mathmountains.org/instructors |website=Math in the Mountains |access-date=31 July 2025}}</ref><ref name="usf bio">{{cite web |title=University of San Francisco College of Arts and Sciences |url=https://www.usfca.edu/faculty/paul-zeitz |website=Paul A. Zeitz Faculty Emeritus |access-date=31 July 2025}}</ref> {{As of|2026}}, he is president of the Organization for Mathematical Engagement & Growth in America (OMEGA).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.omegausa.org/ |title=OMEGA: Organization for Mathematical Engagement & Growth in America |access-date=August 17, 2026}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
In 2003, Zeitz received from the [[Mathematical Association of America]] one of the [[Deborah and Franklin Haimo Awards for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://maa.org/deborah-and-franklin-tepper-haimo-award-for-distinguished-college-or-university-teaching-of-mathematics/ |title=Deborah and Franklin Tepper Haimo Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics |publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]] |access-date=August 17, 2026}}</ref>

Zeitz has a lecture series called ''Art and Craft of Mathematical Problem Solving'' that he made for [[The Teaching Company]] on their platform The Great Courses Plus.<ref>{{cite web |title=Art and Craft of Mathematical Problem Solving |url=https://www.thegreatcoursesplus.com/art-and-craft-of-mathematical-problem-solving |website=The Great Courses Plus |access-date=31 July 2025}}</ref>
